title: Calculation Note — The Online Orders Promised Delivery Date
content:
The promised delivery date of an Online Orders order is the last date of its delivery promise. It is set at placement and set again at dispatch.

## Definition

**At placement**, the promised delivery date is the placement date, moved to the next business day when the order is placed after the service's order cut-off time (Eastern Time) or on a non-business day, plus the service's processing business days plus the service's most transit business days, all counted in business days.

**At dispatch**, the promised delivery date is recomputed as the dispatch date plus the service's most transit business days.

Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding US federal holidays. An order placed exactly at the cut-off time on a business day counts as placed that day; only an order placed after the cut-off moves to the next business day.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Placed | Day the count starts from |
|---|---|
| On a business day, at or before the cut-off | The placement date |
| On a business day, after the cut-off | The next business day |
| On a Saturday, Sunday or US federal holiday | The next business day |

From that day, the business days of processing and the most business days of transit are added together and counted forward.

## Worked examples (hypothetical services and dates; no federal holiday falls in any span)

**Example A.** A service with an order cut-off of 23:59, 1 processing business day and at most 5 transit business days. The order is placed on a Tuesday at 10:00 Eastern Time, before the cut-off, so the count starts from that Tuesday. One plus five gives six business days: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday. The promised delivery date is the Wednesday of the following week.

**Example B.** A service with an order cut-off of 14:00, no processing days and at most 2 transit business days. The order is placed on a Friday at 15:30 Eastern Time, after the cut-off, so the count starts from the next business day, Monday. Two business days later is Wednesday, the promised delivery date.

**Example C.** The service of Example A, but the order is placed on a Saturday at 09:00. Saturday is not a business day, so the count starts from Monday; six business days on is the Tuesday of the following week.

**Example D.** The order of Example A actually leaves the warehouse on the Thursday of its placement week. At dispatch the promise is recomputed as that Thursday plus five business days: the Thursday of the following week.
